title: Gateway telemetry sampling & consent playbook
content:
Purpose:
This note proposes an opinionated playbook for sampling telemetry from customer-managed gateways (edge proxies, customer NATs, transit VPCs) such that:
- we preserve customer privacy and minimize PII collection,
- provide sufficient audit evidence for security/forensics and approval-gate decisions, and
- keep cost and retention bounded for Private deployments.

Why this exists (problem statement):
Private deployments surface two competing needs: customers want control over their network and strict limits on what Redwood can collect; platform and SRE teams need deterministic, searchable evidence when a network change triggers an approval gate or forensic review. Today we either over-collect (blow retention and customer trust) or under-collect (insufficient evidence to validate approvals or investigate incidents).

Goals:
- Define a minimal telemetry schema for change approvals and forensics that is auditable and cryptographically verifiable.
- Introduce sampling heuristics that bias towards anomalous or approval-relevant events while keeping steady-state volumes low.
- Describe a consent-first model: what customers opt-in to, what is mandatory for the product to function, and how we display/record consent.
- Provide concrete examples for retention, encryption, and export controls (KMS, HSM patterns).

Non-goals:
- This doc does NOT define low-level wire formats for every transport (we'll reference WireSpec v1).
- Not a replacement for the full security review; will be used as the product-side proposal for SRE/security review.

Audience:
- Product managers and engineers working on Private (VPC/on-prem) onboarding flows, SRE, security reviewers, and solutions engineering.

High-level approach:
1) Two-tier telemetry: evidence-tickets and telemetry-samples
   - evidence-ticket: small, immutable artifact recorded for each approval-gate decision and operator action (max 6KB). Always captured and stored in customer-scoped immutable ledger. Contains: action-id, actor (delegated subject), local timestamp, approval-gate id, decision, model-version(s) involved, short hash of sampled telemetry bundle, signing key id.
   - telemetry-sample: richer contextual bundle (pcap-lite-like meta + annotated flow records). Captured on a sampling schedule or triggered by heuristics. Stored separately with limited retention and stronger access controls.

2) Sampling heuristics (goal: low steady-state, high signal for anomalies/approvals):
   - Baseline low-rate periodic sampling: 0.1% of connection flows per 10min window (configurable per-customer).
   - Approval-triggered burst: when an approval gate is exercised (new routing, peering, keystore change), capture a 5-minute pre/post window at 100% for affected flows.
   - Anomaly-biased sampling: local edge agent computes lightweight features (unexpected CIDR change, sudden bytes/s flow, new autonomous system seen) and raises a sample token; token weight increases sampling probability for that flow up to 10x.
   - Feedback loop: if a sampled event gets escalated (security/manual review), increase sampling multiplier for same source/actor for next 24h.

3) Privacy and minimization rules:
   - Never capture payloads. Only metadata: source/dest IPs (obfuscated to /64 for IPv6, last octet removed for IPv4 unless triage mandated), ports, protocol, byte counts, timestamps, routing tag, and decision-hash.
   - For customer-managed private deployments where the customer explicitly forbids IP retention, retain only hashed IPs (salted per-customer) in all telemetry and include a reversible escrow process (see escrow section).
   - PII redaction: any header fields that match configured PII regexes are dropped at collection time.

4) Consent model and required opt-ins:
   - Mandatory: evidence-ticket capture for approval-gates. Product will not allow automated approval rollouts without evidence tickets. This is required to provide rollback and audit capabilities.
   - Optional (customer can opt out): steady-state sampling and anomaly telemetry; if opted out, approval-triggered bursts remain mandatory but with stricter minimization (hashed IPs only).
   - Consent artifact: customers must sign a machine-readable consent manifest (JSON) at onboarding; manifest versioning is recorded in the evidence-ticket. Consent changes are handled through an explicit consent-retraction flow (see next-steps).

5) Immutable evidence ledger and signing:
   - Evidence-tickets are appended to the customer ledger (immutable object store + Merkle root published to control plane). Each ticket is signed with a Redwood attestation key and also includes a customer-signed nonce when available (mutual attestation).
   - Ledger retention defaults: 365 days for evidence-tickets, with enterprise tiers configurable to 7+ years. Telemetry-samples default retention: 30 days.

6) Access controls and export rules:
   - Telemetry-samples are encrypted with a customer-scoped KMS key; only people with strong clearance (SRE w/just-in-time approval + customer consent) can request exports.
   - All export requests generate an export-evidence-ticket that is appended to the ledger and triggers a notification to the customer admin contact.

7) Approval gates taxonomy (product-facing):
   - Gate A (Network topology change): any modification to routing tables, peering, or CIDR ranges. Evidence-ticket required. Approval options: automatic (policy), manual (operator), delegated (customer admin).
   - Gate B (Credential/key rotation): keystore or operator-key changes. Always manual with two-party attestation for high-sensitivity keys.
   - Gate C (Capacity/burst permission): allows transient routing/bursting to dedicated clouds. Policy-driven; logs captured at higher sampling rate during bursts.

8) Operational playflows (sketch):
   - Onboarding: capture consent manifest, provision local telemetry agent, provide sample rate defaults and a UI control in Console > Private > Telemetry.
   - Approval event: agent emits evidence-ticket; control plane appends to ledger; if sampling-burst is required, agent sends telemetry-sample bundle to customer-scoped encrypted bucket.
   - Incident triage: on-human escalation, SRE requests telemetry export; customer admin must approve (can pre-authorize support role for org). Export generates export-evidence-ticket.

9) Data formats (high level):
   - evidence-ticket (json-lines, LZ4 compressed): {action_id, actor_id (delegated identities), gate_id, decision, model_version, sample_hash, signing_key, ledger_seq, consent_manifest_ver}
   - telemetry-sample (tar.gz): files: flow_records.csv, routing_events.jsonl, agent_annotations.jsonl, sample_manifest.json

10) Cost & Sizing (rough estimate):
   - 1,000 private deployments, avg 2k flows/min -> baseline sampling 0.1% => ~1.4M flows/day sampled -> estimated raw telemetry-sample storage 130GB/day pre-compression. With 30d retention and compression, budget ~2.5TB.
   - Approval-triggered bursts dominate spikes; design quotas and backpressure to avoid runaway costs.

Implementation notes / engineering considerations:
- Edge agent must be able to compute anomaly features entirely locally; no telemetry sent unless sampled or evidence-ticket required.
- Provide per-customer rate limiters for sampling and burst budgets; surface usage in Console.
- Build an escrow mechanism for reversible hashed IPs: customer-held escrow key + Redwood-held recovery key sealed in HSM; recovery requires dual approval.
- Telemetry ingestion pipeline should tag data with sample_reason (scheduled|approval_burst|anomaly|feedback) for easier query.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Strong vs weak anonymization: do we accept last-octet truncation as sufficient for most customers, or default to salted-hash?
- Retention defaults: security teams want longer evidence retention; customers want shorter. We need tiered pricing and explicit consent.
- Legal needs: what jurisdictions require explicit export permissions before telemetry leaves a customer network? Ask Legal for a matrix.

Mocks / example event (toy):
- Action: add_peering(customer_network: 10.2.0.0/16 -> redwood-edge: 10.200.0.0/16)
- evidence-ticket JSON (toy): action_id: ATC-2026-00421, actor: customer-admin:arjun@acme, gate_id: network-topology-change, decision: approved, sample_hash: sha256:1ab2..., signing_key: rwd-prod-2025-03 (customer consent ver: v1)
- telemetry-sample: flow_records.csv snippet: timestamp,src_ip_masked,dst_ip_masked,src_port,dst_port,proto,bytes
                 2026-01-10T15:02:01Z,10.2.x.x,10.200.x.x,52314,443,TCP,800

Next steps / proposed milestones (approx):
- Week 1–2: Security & Legal review of privacy rules and consent manifest template.
- Week 3–4: Edge-agent prototype for anomaly features + evidence-ticket emission.
- Week 6: Console control wireframe for telemetry toggles and export request flows.
- Week 8–10: Pilot with 2–3 customers; measure sampled volumes and adjust heuristics.

Notes to reviewers (quick):
- Looking for feedback on the sampling multipliers and opt-in model.
- Need Legal to validate consent manifest wording and export constraints.
- Engineering: indicate if the per-customer salt-hash escrow is feasible within HSM constraints.

End of playbook (working doc).
